newsitem.title: USA: Westchester, NY gets $40 mln under watershed pact.
newsitem.headline: Westchester, NY gets $40 mln under watershed pact.

text.p: Westchester County, N.Y., on Monday said that it got $40 million under a new agreement to protect New York City's water system that was reached between the city, Albany and upstate communities.

"This agreement not only protects drinking water, it will allow for economic growth in the watershed communities," said Gov George Pataki, in prepared remarks released by the county. Westchester has said it was getting the first payment under the watershed agreement.

Almost all of the money, $38 million, will be funneled to the East-of-Hudson Water Quality Investments Program, to pay for projects like sewer upgrades. Good Neighbor payments, which total about $1.6 million, will help offset the costs incurred by upstate communities for protecting the New York City watershed.
The pact aims to help the city avoid spending billions of dollars on a sewage filtration plant without stifling economic growth in upstate areas in which the city's 19 reservoirs are located.
The city agreed to spend $260 million to buy land around the reservoirs and $334 million on new programs with local communities, in addition to other costs.
New York City Comptroller Alan Hevesi has estimated the agreement could cost the city about $2.2 billion.
